headlines.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez says she hasn’t ruled out a potential run for president or Senate in 2028
headlines.description: The New York representative said “anything is possible at this juncture” when asked whether she’d thought about running for Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s seat.

headlines.title: Sen. Jim Banks says Rep. Max Miller should drop his re-election bid if allegations are true
headlines.description: The Indiana Republican is the latest GOP lawmaker to call on Miller, R-Ohio, to step aside in the wake of domestic violence allegations, which he has denied.

headlines.title: Richard Nixon reflects on Watergate and his legacy: Meet the Press Archive
headlines.description: APRIL 10, 1988 — Former President Richard Nixon joined Meet the Press years after resigning from office on August 9, 1974, after five men were arrested for breaking into the Democratic National Committee headquarters at the Watergate complex in Washington, D.C. in June of that year.

headlines.title: Abdul El-Sayed says he spoke with Obama after primary win, hopes he’ll campaign for him
headlines.description: In an interview with Meet the Press, Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed says he “really enjoyed” his recent conversation with former President Barack Obama and hopes he’ll campaign with him ahead of the general election.

headlines.title: Can Progressive Democrats Win in the 2026 Midterm Elections?
headlines.description: Meet the Press moderator Kristen Welker joins Sunday TODAY’s Willie Geist to discuss how Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed’s victory in Michigan sets up a battle internally between centrist Democrats and progressives. “The challenge for him will be winning over those who voted for his opponent and moderate and independent voters who can sway the entire election,” Kristen says.

headlines.title: Trump imposes 50% tariffs on dairy, alcohol, and cars from Canada
headlines.description: The Trump administration imposed 50% tariffs on three categories of imports from Canada, dairy, alcohol, and cars, citing discriminatory actions. NBC News' Monica Alba reports on how Trump is also considering additional tariffs due to the Canadian wildfires.

headlines.title: Abdul El-Sayed says he hopes to campaign with Obama after ‘warm and inspiring’ call
headlines.description: Top Democrats, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, have lined up behind El-Sayed after supporting his rival in the primary.

headlines.title: Hunter Biden says Joe Biden’s cancer has spread
headlines.description: Former President Joe Biden’s son, Hunter Biden, said his father’s cancer is spreading in what he described as a “very debilitating” state.

headlines.title: Senate confirms Todd Blanche as attorney general after weeks of uncertainty
headlines.description: The Senate confirmed Todd Blanche as U.S. attorney general early Saturday in a mostly party-line vote, capping off weeks of uncertainty and despite bipartisan concerns about his ability to run a Justice Department independent of President Donald Trump’s impulses.

headlines.title: Senate passes short-term bill to prevent a shutdown before the midterm elections
headlines.description: WASHINGTON — The Senate voted 90-6 early Saturday to pass a short-term funding bill to remove the threat of a government shutdown before the midterm elections.

headlines.title: Fault lines for both parties emerge after Michigan’s primaries: From the Politics Desk
headlines.description: In today’s edition, Kristen Welker looks ahead to November in swing state Michigan after this week’s primary battles.

headlines.title: Sen. Bill Cassidy, a critical Republican holdout, backs Todd Blanche for attorney general
headlines.description: Republican Sens. Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Susan Collins of Maine said they would oppose Blanche. But Cassidy’s support means he will likely be confirmed.
